___

**DEF**)
Let $R$ be a commutative [[Ring|ring]] with unity and $a \in R$.
The ideal $\{ra|r\in R\}$, all multiples of $a$ is the **principal ideal generated by a** and is denoted by $\left< a \right>$.
An ideal $N$ of $R$ is **principal ideal** if $N = \left< a \right>$ for some $a \in R$.

___

* Why this set is ideal?
See the definition of [[Ideal|ideal]].

**EXAMPLE**)

* Every ideal of $\mathbb{Z}$ is of the form $n\mathbb{Z}$, which is generated by $n$, so every ideal of $\mathbb{Z}$ is a principal ideal.

* The ideal $\left< x \right>$ of $F[x]$ consists of all polynomials in $F[x]$ having zero constant term.
